title: Do vaccinated cases transmit measles? A systematic review and meta-analysis
abstract: INTRODUCTION: We reviewed evidence on whether vaccinated individuals can transmit measles and conducted a meta-analysis to understand transmission characteristics. METHODS: We searched and extracted data from peer-reviewed and gray literature and included studies reporting measles transmission events from vaccinated individuals. We meta-analyzed the data to calculate the median number of transmissions from vaccinated cases by measles burden, number of doses, and time since first and last dose. RESULTS: We identified 11,911 peer-reviewed and 22 gray literature records and included 33 articles in our review. Seventy individuals who had received 1 or more doses of measles-containing vaccine transmitted measles virus, resulting in 237 secondary cases. Vaccinated transmitters in eliminated areas were older (median age of 19 years (IQR: 3, 21)) than those in non-eliminated areas (median age 16 years; IQR 13, 18) (p = 0.12). Additionally, 91% (30/33) of studies provided data on subsequent transmission generations, leading to 812 measles cases traced back to vaccinated individuals, with a median of 4 (IQR: 1, 10) cases per vaccinated transmitter. CONCLUSION: Measles transmissions from vaccinated cases, although relatively uncommon, must be considered in public health investigations, as such transmissions can contribute to outbreaks.

The review included 33 articles from 11,911 peer-reviewed and 22 gray literature records. title: Operational drivers of measles outbreaks in Uganda: a multi-district outbreak causality analysis, July 2025– March 2026
abstract: Abstract Background Measles outbreaks in Uganda persist despite the availability of an effective vaccine, suggesting persistent immunity gaps and health system weaknesses. We conducted a multi-district outbreak causality analysis (OCA) to identify programmatic and health-system contributors to measles outbreaks and inform measles elimination programming. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional mixed-methods OCA across 12 affected districts in Uganda (2025–2026), guided by the World Health Organization framework. We reviewed measles case investigation reports and triangulated findings with qualitative interviews with district health teams, health workers, surveillance and immunisation staff, community leaders, Village Health Teams, and caregivers. We deductively analysed data to identify causal pathways and contributing factors. Findings were organized into four prespecified analytical themes: immunization service delivery, caregiver access and demand, surveillance and case detection, and outbreak preparedness and response. Results The 12 districts reported 1,302 cases, including 80 laboratory-confirmed cases and 10 suspected deaths (case-fatality rate: 0.77%); 46.5% (n=606) occurred among children aged 18– 59 months. Most cases (65.3%) occurred in unvaccinated children, versus 1.0% in children with both measles-rubella (MR) doses. Across districts, incomplete MR2 implementation, irregular outreach, inconsistent fixed-site vaccination, weak follow-up of children who missed vaccination, and transport and distance barriers contributed to persistent immunity gaps. Low clinical suspicion, limited engagement of Village Health Teams, laboratory and surveillance-information bottlenecks, absence of pre-positioned response plans, delayed response activation, and inadequate isolation capacity further limited early detection and control. Conclusion Measles outbreaks were driven primarily by missed vaccination, especially incomplete delivery of the two-dose MR schedule, compounded by access barriers, delayed case detection, and limited outbreak preparedness. Strengthening routine MR1 and MR2 delivery, targeted catch-up vaccination, community-linked surveillance, and pre-positioned district response plans with clear activation triggers will be critical to closing immunity gaps and accelerating measles elimination in Uganda.

source_body_en: Abstract Background Measles outbreaks in Uganda persist despite the availability of an effective vaccine, suggesting persistent immunity gaps and health system weaknesses. We conducted a multi-district outbreak causality analysis (OCA) to identify programmatic and health-system contributors to measles outbreaks and inform measles elimination programming. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional mixed-methods OCA across 12 affected districts in Uganda (2025–2026), guided by the World Health Organization framework. We reviewed measles case investigation reports and triangulated findings with qualitative interviews with district health teams, health workers, surveillance and immunisation staff, community leaders, Village Health Teams, and caregivers. We deductively analysed data to identify causal pathways and contributing factors. Findings were organized into four prespecified analytical themes: immunization service delivery, caregiver access and demand, surveillance and case detection, and outbreak preparedness and response. Results The 12 districts reported 1,302 cases, including 80 laboratory-confirmed cases and 10 suspected deaths (case-fatality rate: 0.77%); 46.5% (n=606) occurred among children aged 18– 59 months. Most cases (65.3%) occurred in unvaccinated children, versus 1.0% in children with both measles-rubella (MR) doses. Across districts, incomplete MR2 implementation, irregular outreach, inconsistent fixed-site vaccination, weak follow-up of children who missed vaccination, and transport and distance barriers contributed to persistent immunity gaps. Low clinical suspicion, limited engagement of Village Health Teams, laboratory and surveillance-information bottlenecks, absence of pre-positioned response plans, delayed response activation, and inadequate isolation capacity further limited early detection and control. Conclusion Measles outbreaks were driven primarily by missed vaccination, especially incomplete delivery of the two-dose MR schedule, compounded by access barriers, delayed case detection, and limited outbreak preparedness. Strengthening routine MR1 and MR2 delivery, targeted catch-up vaccination, community-linked surveillance, and pre-positioned district response plans with clear activation triggers will be critical to closing immunity gaps and accelerating measles elimination in Uganda.

title: Integrated Computational Design and Molecular Dynamics Evaluation of Novel siRNAs Targeting the Hemagglutinin Gene of Measles Virus
abstract: Abstract Despite the availability of an effective vaccine, measles virus (MV) remains a major global health concern because no approved antiviral therapeutics currently exist. RNA interference (RNAi) is a promising antiviral strategy, but studies targeting the conserved MV hemagglutinin (H) gene are limited. In this study, an integrated computational pipeline was used to identify and evaluate novel siRNA candidates targeting the MV H gene. At first, 96 MV strains were used to perform multiple sequence alignment (MSA) to generate a consensus sequence, and the phylogenetic tree demonstrated limited genetic divergence among the strains. 11 siRNA candidates were then designed and screened for off-target effects. Subsequently, they were subjected to thermodynamic analysis, secondary and tertiary structure prediction, hybridization energy evaluation, and molecular docking against human Argonaute-2 (hAgo2). The docking results showed that S3, S4, and S7 displayed docking scores of -367.22, − 349.03, and − 383.07 kcal/mol with the most favorable binding orientation within the catalytic PIWI domain of hAgo2. The three selected candidates maintained stable structural behavior throughout 100 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. These computational analyses indicate that the S3, S4, and S7 may serve as promising siRNA candidates against the MV H gene, which require further in vitro gene silencing assays and in vivo validation.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Despite the availability of an effective vaccine, measles virus (MV) remains a major global health concern because no approved antiviral therapeutics currently exist, and RNA interference (RNAi) studies targeting the conserved MV hemagglutinin (H) gene are limited.

analysis.methods: Eleven siRNA candidates were designed and screened for off-target effects, followed by thermodynamic analysis, secondary and tertiary structure prediction, hybridization energy evaluation, and molecular docking against human Argonaute-2 (hAgo2), with stability assessed via 100 ns molecular dynamics (MD) simulations.
analysis.main_results: The docking results showed that siRNA candidates S3, S4, and S7 displayed docking scores of -367.22, -349.03, and -383.07 kcal/mol, respectively, with favorable binding orientation within the catalytic PIWI domain of hAgo2, and maintained stable structural behavior throughout the simulations.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret these findings as indicating that S3, S4, and S7 may serve as promising siRNA candidates against the MV H gene, representing a novel computational approach to antiviral development for measles.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings could inform the design of future antiviral strategies targeting measles, potentially addressing the unmet need for approved therapeutics and supporting the development of RNAi-based interventions.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to computational predictions and simulations, with no in vitro or in vivo validation reported, indicating low strength and necessitating further experimental confirmation before clinical relevance can be assessed.

analysis.summary_en: This computational study aimed to address the lack of approved antiviral therapeutics for measles virus (MV) by designing and evaluating siRNA candidates targeting the conserved hemagglutinin (H) gene. Using 96 MV strains, the authors performed multiple sequence alignment and phylogenetic analysis to identify conserved regions, followed by the design of 11 siRNA candidates. These candidates underwent thermodynamic analysis, structural prediction, docking against human Argonaute-2, and 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations. The top three candidates (S3, S4, S7) demonstrated favorable docking scores and stable structural behavior, suggesting potential as antiviral agents. However, the study is limited to computational predictions without experimental validation, and the evidence strength is low, requiring in vitro and in vivo studies to confirm efficacy and safety.

abstract_zh: 摘要:尽管存在有效的 疫苗,但 麻疹病毒 (MV) 仍然是全球主要的健康问题,因为目前尚无批准的 抗病毒药物 疗法。RNA 干扰 (RNAi) 是一种很有前景的 抗病毒药物 策略,但针对保守的 MV 血凝素 (H) 基因的研究有限。在本研究中,使用集成计算流程来识别和评估针对 MV H 基因的新型 siRNA 候选物。首先,使用96个MV毒株进行多重序列比对(MSA)以生成共有序列,系统发育树显示毒株之间的遗传差异有限。然后设计并筛选 11 种 siRNA 候选物的脱靶效应。随后,对它们进行了热力学分析、二级和三级结构预测、杂交能量评估以及与人类Argonaute-2(hAgo2)的分子对接。对接结果显示,S3、S4和S7的对接分数分别为-367.22、- 349.03和- 383.07 kcal/mol,在hAgo2的催化PIWI结构域内具有最有利的结合方向。选定的三个候选者在 100 ns 分子动力学 (MD) 模拟过程中保持稳定的结构行为。这些计算分析表明,S3、S4 和 S7 可能作为针对 MV H 基因的有希望的 siRNA 候选物,这需要进一步的体外基因沉默测定和体内验证。

title: Otimização da logística laboratorial e monitoramento de amostras de sangue para diagnóstico do sarampo no Tocantins Optimization of laboratory logistics and blood sample monitoring for measles diagnosis in Tocantins Optimización de la logística de laboratorio y monitoreo de muestras de sangre para diagnóstico de sarampión en Tocantins
abstract: Efficient laboratory logistics is a decisive factor for the quality of health surveillance, especially in territorially extensive settings with structural limitations, such as the state of Tocantins, Brazil. This article analyzes a proposal to optimize the logistics network and monitoring of blood samples intended for measles diagnosis within the Central Public Health Laboratory of Tocantins. The study was based on an institutional diagnosis that identified transport delays, lack of standardized packaging procedures, sample degradation due to failures in the cold chain, lack of traceability, and high costs associated with individualized transportation. Methodologically, this is an applied, qualitative, and descriptive study grounded in institutional empirical data, bibliographic review, and technical-propositional formulation. The results indicate that adopting an integrated logistics model, with regional hubs, route reorganization, operational protocols, and performance indicators, may reduce losses, improve sample reliability, lower operational costs, and strengthen intergovernmental governance between the state and municipalities. title: Genetic characterization of production strains of measles, rubella, and mumps viruses by high-throughput sequencing
abstract: Spontaneous mutations often arise and accumulate in the genome of RNA-containing viruses, for example measles, rubella and mumps. Modern requirements for the production of vaccine products containing live vaccine viruses suggest control of the genetic stability of production strains. The method of high throughput sequencing allows to determine all mutations arisen in viral population, and to assess genetic stability of production strains. Analysis of nucleotide sequence of the genomes of seed and production strains of measles (Leningrad-16), rubella (RA27/3) and mumps (Leningrad-3) viruses, in comparison with the reference nucleotide sequences of vaccine strains genomes (submitted in the Gen-Bank database). MATERIALS AND METHODS. Production strains of vaccines (measles culture live, rubella culture live and mumps culture live) were used in this study. Whole genome sequencing was performed using the MGI DNBSEQ G-400 and Illumina NextSeq2000 genetic analyzers. When processing and analyzing the sequencing data, the following programs and tools were used: FastQC v.0.12.1, FastP v.0.23.4, BWA-MEM2 v.2.2.1, VizCoV tool. Analysis of single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) within the viral population in the studied samples revealed a number of minor variants that, and after further accumulation, may lead to changes in the consensus sequences of the vaccine strains proteins. For the studied measles virus samples, no SNPs were found in the main measles virus antigen H protein, however, a nonsynonymous polymorphism was detected in the F protein, occurring in 30.0–40.9% of the viral genomes. SNPs were found in the capsid protein C and in the surface glycoprotein E2 rubella virus, occurring in the viral population with a frequency of up to 30%. SNPs were found in surface antigens hemagglutinin neuraminidase HN and fusion protein F of mumps virus, occurring in the genomes of less than 20% of viral population. Mutations in the genomes of production strains that could affect the immunogenicity of measles, rubella, and mumps vaccines were not detected. The identified set of minor variants with a frequency of occurrence in viral population of more than 10%, which, with further accumulation, can lead to changes in the consensus sequences of vaccine strains, makes the monitoring of vaccine strains stability using high-throughput sequencing relevant.

title: Association of Measles IgG Antibody Titers with Thoracic CT Severity in Hospitalized Patients with COVID-19
abstract: Abstract Background Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has a broad clinical spectrum ranging from mild respiratory symptoms to severe pneumonia and death. Previous studies have suggested that pre-existing immunity against measles may influence immune responses during SARS-CoV-2 infection; however, the clinical significance of anti-measles IgG titers in COVID-19 remains unclear. Therefore, we aimed to investigate the association between anti-measles IgG titers, clinical severity, COVID-19 Mortality Rate (CMR) score, intensive care unit (ICU) requirement, and mortality in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. Material and Methods This cross-sectional study included 153 hospitalized COVID-19 patients (86 males and 67 females). Disease severity was classified according to the NIH COVID-19 Treatment Guidelines. Anti-measles IgG levels were measured using an indirect ELISA assay. Mortality risk was assessed using the COVID-19 Mortality Rate (CMR) score. Results Higher anti-measles IgG titers were observed in patients with severe COVID-19 and severe thoracic CT involvement compared with patients with milder disease. Anti-measles IgG titers were significantly higher in patients with severe CT involvement compared with those with non-severe involvement and remained independently associated with severe thoracic CT involvement after adjustment for clinical and laboratory parameters. However, anti-measles IgG levels were not independently associated with mortality or ICU admission. Non-survivors were older, had longer hospital stays, higher CMR scores, and lower admission SpO2 levels compared with survivors. Similarly, patients requiring ICU admission had higher CMR scores and more severe thoracic CT involvement. Conclusion Higher anti-measles IgG titers were independently associated with severe thoracic CT involvement in hospitalized COVID-19 patients. These findings suggest that anti-measles IgG levels may represent a potential immunological marker associated with pulmonary disease severity rather than a direct marker of mortality risk. Further prospective studies with larger populations are needed to clarify the clinical significance of anti-measles IgG responses in COVID-19.

title: Clinical and epidemiological profile of suspected and laboratory-confirmed measles cases in South Kivu, Democratic Republic of the Congo, 2023
abstract: Measles remains a major public health challenge in many low-resource settings, despite repeated vaccination efforts. In 2023, a resurgence of suspected measles cases was reported in South Kivu Province (Democratic Republic of Congo) following a mass vaccination campaign targeting children aged 6–59 months. This study aimed to describe the clinical and epidemiological characteristics of suspected measles cases and to identify factors associated with measles IgM positivity in the post-campaign period. A cross-sectional study was conducted among children aged 6–59 months presenting with clinical signs of measles in five health zones most affected by the outbreak (Kalehe, Minova, Idjwi, Miti-Murhesa, and Kalonge). Suspected cases were enrolled exhaustively from line lists provided by local health authorities. After obtaining parental consent, blood samples were collected and tested for measles and rubella IgM antibodies at the National Institute for Biomedical Research (INRB). Data were analyzed using R version 4.3.3. Logistic regression was used to identify characteristics associated with measles IgM positivity among suspected cases. Of the 82 children tested, 39 (48%) were positive for measles IgM. Among the 43 IgM-negative children, 8 (18%) were rubella IgM positive. In adjusted analyses, measles IgM positivity showed an evidence of an association with male parental decision-making regarding child vaccination (aOR :7.22; 95% CI: 1.64–43.2; p = 0.015) and others workers (aOR: 8.28; 95%CI:1.19-48; p = < 0.008). Despite reported high administrative vaccination coverage, measles continues to circulate among children in South Kivu. Strengthening immunization service quality, improving outreach to unvaccinated children, and engaging male parents and others workers may enhance vaccine acceptance and reduce measles transmission in the post-campaign period.

title_zh: 2023 年刚果民主共和国南基伍省疑似和实验室确诊 麻疹 病例的临床和流行病学概况
source_body_en: Measles remains a major public health challenge in many low-resource settings, despite repeated vaccination efforts. In 2023, a resurgence of suspected measles cases was reported in South Kivu Province (Democratic Republic of Congo) following a mass vaccination campaign targeting children aged 6–59 months. This study aimed to describe the clinical and epidemiological characteristics of suspected measles cases and to identify factors associated with measles IgM positivity in the post-campaign period. A cross-sectional study was conducted among children aged 6–59 months presenting with clinical signs of measles in five health zones most affected by the outbreak (Kalehe, Minova, Idjwi, Miti-Murhesa, and Kalonge). Suspected cases were enrolled exhaustively from line lists provided by local health authorities. After obtaining parental consent, blood samples were collected and tested for measles and rubella IgM antibodies at the National Institute for Biomedical Research (INRB). Data were analyzed using R version 4.3.3. Logistic regression was used to identify characteristics associated with measles IgM positivity among suspected cases. Of the 82 children tested, 39 (48%) were positive for measles IgM. Among the 43 IgM-negative children, 8 (18%) were rubella IgM positive. In adjusted analyses, measles IgM positivity showed an evidence of an association with male parental decision-making regarding child vaccination (aOR :7.22; 95% CI: 1.64–43.2; p = 0.015) and others workers (aOR: 8.28; 95%CI:1.19-48; p = < 0.008). Despite reported high administrative vaccination coverage, measles continues to circulate among children in South Kivu. Strengthening immunization service quality, improving outreach to unvaccinated children, and engaging male parents and others workers may enhance vaccine acceptance and reduce measles transmission in the post-campaign period.

title: Universal screening for measles immunity during pregnancy: a cost-effectiveness analysis.
abstract: BACKGROUND: Measles is a highly contagious illness capable of causing significant morbidity and mortality, including adverse pregnancy outcomes. Routine screening for measles immunity is not currently recommended during pregnancy. Given the increasing frequency of measles outbreaks nationally and globally, awareness of measles immunity status can influence management of pregnant individuals who incur measles exposures, and offer an opportunity for postpartum or preconception vaccination. OBJECTIVES: We sought to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of universal screening for measles immunity during pregnancy in the United States. STUDY DESIGN: A decision-analytic model was constructed to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of universal screening for measles immunity during pregnancy compared to usual care (ie, no screening for measles immunity). The outcome of the decision analysis was quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) of the pregnant person. Model inputs were derived from the literature. Our model ran over two pregnancy cycles with a willingness-to-pay threshold of $100,000 per QALY. Total costs and QALYs were used to measure the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) of universal measles screening compared with usual care. Sensitivity analyses were conducted to evaluate the robustness of the results. RESULTS: Universal screening for measles immunity was the dominant strategy. Using a measles exposure rate of 0.1% to reflect the highest risk areas, the ICER of universal screening versus no screening was $166.46/QALY. Tornado sensitivity analyses demonstrated that the cost of measles screening and the probability of measles exposure had greatest impact on the cost-effectiveness of the screening strategy. When varying the measles exposure rate from 0.001-0.1%, screening remained the dominant strategy. During Monte Carlo simulation, measles screening for immunity during pregnancy was cost-saving and increased QALYs in 99.83% of simulations. CONCLUSIONS: Universal screening for measles immunity during pregnancy is a cost-effective strategy. We argue for adoption of universal measles screening during pregnancy in the United States. Until adopted, providers should consider screening their pregnant patients and recommending postpartum vaccination. If implemented, further study will be needed to assess the actual benefit of universal screening.

However, the study relies on literature-derived inputs and does not include real-world data, limiting its evidence strength to moderate. The findings suggest that universal screening could be a valuable tool in managing measles risks during pregnancy.

title_zh: 怀孕期间 麻疹 免疫力的普遍筛查:成本效益分析。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Measles is a highly contagious illness capable of causing significant morbidity and mortality, including adverse pregnancy outcomes. Routine screening for measles immunity is not currently recommended during pregnancy. Given the increasing frequency of measles outbreaks nationally and globally, awareness of measles immunity status can influence management of pregnant individuals who incur measles exposures, and offer an opportunity for postpartum or preconception vaccination. OBJECTIVES: We sought to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of universal screening for measles immunity during pregnancy in the United States. STUDY DESIGN: A decision-analytic model was constructed to evaluate the cost-effectiveness of universal screening for measles immunity during pregnancy compared to usual care (ie, no screening for measles immunity). The outcome of the decision analysis was quality-adjusted life years (QALYs) of the pregnant person. Model inputs were derived from the literature. Our model ran over two pregnancy cycles with a willingness-to-pay threshold of $100,000 per QALY. Total costs and QALYs were used to measure the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER) of universal measles screening compared with usual care. Sensitivity analyses were conducted to evaluate the robustness of the results. RESULTS: Universal screening for measles immunity was the dominant strategy. Using a measles exposure rate of 0.1% to reflect the highest risk areas, the ICER of universal screening versus no screening was $166.46/QALY. Tornado sensitivity analyses demonstrated that the cost of measles screening and the probability of measles exposure had greatest impact on the cost-effectiveness of the screening strategy. When varying the measles exposure rate from 0.001-0.1%, screening remained the dominant strategy. During Monte Carlo simulation, measles screening for immunity during pregnancy was cost-saving and increased QALYs in 99.83% of simulations. CONCLUSIONS: Universal screening for measles immunity during pregnancy is a cost-effective strategy. We argue for adoption of universal measles screening during pregnancy in the United States. Until adopted, providers should consider screening their pregnant patients and recommending postpartum vaccination. If implemented, further study will be needed to assess the actual benefit of universal screening.

title: Characterizing Measles IgG-related Seroprevalence in the US Veteran Population during the 2025 West Texas outbreak.
abstract: BACKGROUND: The 2025 United States (US) measles outbreak supports concerns that measles may have significant resurgences. The study's objectives were to characterize measles serologic testing rates, estimate measles IgG seronegativity rates, and determine independent variables associated with seronegativity across the US Veterans Health Administration (VHA). METHODS: A nationwide retrospective, observational study was conducted collecting data from veterans with measles IgG antibody testing performed from January through June in 2024 (pre-outbreak) and 2025 (outbreak). Endpoints included determining independent variables associated with 1) measles IgG testing within the outbreak period versus the pre-outbreak period, and 2) measles IgG seronegativity within the outbreak period. RESULTS: 16,446 veterans had measles IgG testing in the outbreak period, a 60.3% increase in the testing rate compared to the non-outbreak period. Seronegativity was found in 1,220 (11.9%) veterans in the non-outbreak period and 1,509 veterans (9.18%) in the outbreak period (p<0.0001). Independent variables associated with seronegativity included age 64 years or below (OR 5.65, 95% CI 4.59-6.94), Janus kinase inhibitor use (OR 3.54, CI 1.24-10.1), and immunodeficient condition (OR 3.10, CI 2.34-4.11). CONCLUSIONS: As measles reemerges, certain populations were identified that may be at higher risk of infection and transmission, particularly those with immune compromise.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Measles resurgence in the US raised concerns about population immunity gaps. The study addressed knowledge gaps on measles IgG seronegativity rates and testing patterns in the US veteran population during the 2025 outbreak.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A nationwide retrospective observational study was conducted using the US Veterans Health Administration (VHA) database. Veterans with measles IgG antibody testing performed from January through June in 2024 (pre-outbreak) and 2025 (outbreak) were included.
analysis.methods: Data were collected on measles IgG testing and serostatus during pre-outbreak and outbreak periods. Independent variables associated with seronegativity were determined using statistical models.
analysis.main_results: Measles IgG testing increased by 60.3% during the outbreak period (16,446 veterans tested). Seronegativity was 11.9% in the non-outbreak period and 9.18% in the outbreak period (p<0.0001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as identifying populations at higher risk of infection and transmission, particularly those with immune compromise. They highlighted the need for targeted interventions in these groups.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform vaccination strategies and targeted serologic screening in veterans, especially those with immunodeficiency or on Janus kinase inhibitors, to mitigate measles resurgence risks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study's retrospective design and reliance on existing VHA data may limit generalizability and introduce selection bias. The evidence strength is assessed as moderate due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This nationwide retrospective study assessed measles IgG seroprevalence in the US veteran population during the 2025 outbreak. Testing rates rose by 60.3% compared to the pre-outbreak period, with seronegativity decreasing from 11.9% to 9.18%. Independent risk factors for seronegativity included age ≤64 years, Janus kinase inhibitor use, and immunodeficient conditions. The authors conclude that targeted interventions are needed for high-risk groups to address measles resurgence. Limitations include retrospective design and potential selection bias, warranting cautious interpretation.

analysis_en.study_design_and_population: A nationwide retrospective observational study was conducted using the US Veterans Health Administration (VHA) database. Veterans with measles IgG antibody testing performed from January through June in 2024 (pre-outbreak) and 2025 (outbreak) were included.
analysis_en.methods: Data were collected on measles IgG testing and serostatus during pre-outbreak and outbreak periods. Independent variables associated with seronegativity were determined using statistical models.
analysis_en.main_results: Measles IgG testing increased by 60.3% during the outbreak period (16,446 veterans tested). Seronegativity was 11.9% in the non-outbreak period and 9.18% in the outbreak period (p<0.0001).

title_zh: 描述 2025 年西德克萨斯州 麻疹 期间美国退伍军人群体中 麻疹 IgG 相关 血清流行率 的特征。
source_body_en: BACKGROUND: The 2025 United States (US) measles outbreak supports concerns that measles may have significant resurgences. The study's objectives were to characterize measles serologic testing rates, estimate measles IgG seronegativity rates, and determine independent variables associated with seronegativity across the US Veterans Health Administration (VHA). METHODS: A nationwide retrospective, observational study was conducted collecting data from veterans with measles IgG antibody testing performed from January through June in 2024 (pre-outbreak) and 2025 (outbreak). Endpoints included determining independent variables associated with 1) measles IgG testing within the outbreak period versus the pre-outbreak period, and 2) measles IgG seronegativity within the outbreak period. RESULTS: 16,446 veterans had measles IgG testing in the outbreak period, a 60.3% increase in the testing rate compared to the non-outbreak period. Seronegativity was found in 1,220 (11.9%) veterans in the non-outbreak period and 1,509 veterans (9.18%) in the outbreak period (p<0.0001). Independent variables associated with seronegativity included age 64 years or below (OR 5.65, 95% CI 4.59-6.94), Janus kinase inhibitor use (OR 3.54, CI 1.24-10.1), and immunodeficient condition (OR 3.10, CI 2.34-4.11). CONCLUSIONS: As measles reemerges, certain populations were identified that may be at higher risk of infection and transmission, particularly those with immune compromise.

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用美国退伍军人健康管理局 (VHA) 数据库进行了一项全国性回顾性观察研究。包括 2024 年(麻疹 之前)和 2025 年(暴发)1 月至 6 月进行过 麻疹 IgG 抗体测试的退伍军人。
analysis_zh.methods: 在 麻疹 之前和 暴发 期间收集 麻疹 IgG 测试和血清状态的数据。使用统计模型确定与血清阴性相关的自变量。
analysis_zh.main_results: 麻疹 IgG 检测在 麻疹 期间增加了 60.3%(检测了 16,446 名退伍军人)。非 暴发 期间的血清阴性率为 11.9%,暴发 期间的血清阴性率为 9.18%(p<0.0001)。

title: Measles in Poland in 2024
abstract: Background Measles remains one of the most contagious viral diseases, and its elimination in the WHO European Region requires maintaining high vaccination rates and effective epidemiological surveillance. Following the COVID-19 pandemic, many European countries, including Poland, are seeing a renewed increase in the number of cases. Objective The aim of the study was to assess the epidemiological situation of measles in Poland in 2024, taking into account the vaccination status of the population against measles and the degree of implementation of the World Health Organization (WHO) measles eradication program in Poland. Material and methods The epidemiological situation of measles in Poland in 2024 was assessed using data obtained from the national infectious disease surveillance system, recorded by the local sanitary and epidemiological stations in the Epibaza system. Additional information was obtained from the annual bulletins “Infectious Diseases and Poisonings in Poland” and “Vaccinations in Poland” for the years 2015-2024. Results In 2024, an increase in the number of measles cases was recorded in Poland. A total of 272 cases were reported (incidence rate 0.72/100,000), compared with 35 cases in 2023 (0.09/100,000), representing representing more than a sevenfold increase, largely due to the very low number of cases in the previous year. The rise in reported cases was associated with several measles outbreaks, primarily in the Mazowieckie and Dolnośląskie voivodeships. Altogether, 23 outbreaks were identified. Analysis in relation to the pre-COVID-19 period (2019) indicates a persistently lower incidence rate. In 2019, 1,502 cases were reported (3.31/100,000). Compared with the median for 2018-2022, the number of cases in 2024 was more than eight times higher. The highest incidence was observed among children aged 0-9 years. The increase in cases and hospitalizations coincided with a decline in vaccination coverage below 95%, increasing the risk of local outbreaks. Conclusions Maintaining measles elimination in Poland requires sustaining at least 95% coverage with two doses of the measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine. This should be supported by continued routine immunization, catch-up vaccination of susceptible individuals, and further strengthening of epidemiological and laboratory surveillance, including molecular characterization of circulating measles viruses.

title: Discrete state-structured epidemic model with varying susceptibility and infectivity and its application to the measles outbreak in the United States
abstract: Host individuals with vaccinations for infectious diseases often transition among different states of susceptibility and infectivity. Thus, we derive a class of epidemic models in which susceptible and infected individuals have a discrete set of susceptibility and infectivity states, respectively. Our model is based on double-dose vaccination and accounts for all possible state transitions between states. A comprehensive mathematical analysis of the proposed model is conducted, including assessing the control reproduction number and the global dynamical behaviors of the solutions. By using an improved affine-invariant ensemble Markov chain Monte Carlo method, we also fit the model with measles case data in the United States. The results indicate that despite high vaccination coverage and efficacy rates, sporadic or small-scale measles outbreaks still occur. This suggests that reliance solely on vaccination policies is insufficient to fully interrupt its transmission chain. Consequently, enhancing the diagnosis rate of measles cases is another crucial measure for controlling measles transmission and outbreaks, building upon existing vaccination efforts.

title: Quantifying the impact of time-delayed reporting and supportive care in measles outbreak: A simulation approach for Texas, USA.
abstract: This study examines how time delays in vaccination response, case reporting, and access to supportive care influence measles transmission during the recent outbreak in Texas, USA. We develop a delay-based compartmental model that captures both biological and operational features of measles control and calibrate it using Texas reported Measles incidence data from January 20 to May 27, 2025. Analytical and numerical results show that delays in reporting and intervention can substantially weaken outbreak control, allowing transmission to persist even in highly vaccinated populations. In contrast, timely case detection, improved vaccination uptake, and access to supportive care significantly reduce transmission and can drive the effective reproduction number below unity. These findings highlight the critical role of minimizing reporting and healthcare delays alongside sustained immunization efforts to prevent measles resurgence and support elimination goals in Texas and similar settings.

title_zh: 量化 麻疹 麻疹 中延时报告和支持性护理的影响:美国德克萨斯州的模拟方法。
source_body_en: This study examines how time delays in vaccination response, case reporting, and access to supportive care influence measles transmission during the recent outbreak in Texas, USA. We develop a delay-based compartmental model that captures both biological and operational features of measles control and calibrate it using Texas reported Measles incidence data from January 20 to May 27, 2025. Analytical and numerical results show that delays in reporting and intervention can substantially weaken outbreak control, allowing transmission to persist even in highly vaccinated populations. In contrast, timely case detection, improved vaccination uptake, and access to supportive care significantly reduce transmission and can drive the effective reproduction number below unity. These findings highlight the critical role of minimizing reporting and healthcare delays alongside sustained immunization efforts to prevent measles resurgence and support elimination goals in Texas and similar settings.
abstract_zh: 本研究探讨了最近在美国德克萨斯州发生的 麻疹 期间,疫苗接种 反应、病例报告和获得支持性护理的时间延迟如何影响 麻疹 传播。我们开发了一种基于延迟的区室模型,该模型捕获了 麻疹 控制的生物学和操作特征,并使用德克萨斯州报告的 2025 年 1 月 20 日至 5 月 27 日的 麻疹 发病率 数据对其进行校准。分析和数值结果表明,报告和干预的延迟会大大削弱 麻疹 控制,使 传播 即使在高度接种疫苗的情况下也能持续存在人口。相比之下,及时发现病例、提高 疫苗接种 的吸收率以及获得支持性护理可显着减少 传播 的数量,并可使有效繁殖数低于统一值。这些发现强调了最大限度地减少报告和医疗延误以及持续免疫工作对于防止 麻疹 卷土重来并支持德克萨斯州和类似地区消除 麻疹 目标的关键作用。

title: Infection with measles virus induces leukopenia and rash in a humanized immune system mouse model
abstract: Abstract Humans are the natural hosts of the measles virus (MV). With the exception of non-human primates, no other animal species are naturally susceptible to MV infection. Thus, no small animal models exist to study the mechanisms of MV pathogenicity. The aim of the present study was to establish a small animal model of MV infection using NOD/LtSz-scid/IL2Rγ null (NSG) immunodeficient mice implanted with human-cord-blood-derived CD34 + cells and to evaluate its suitability as a measles model. Upon infecting the humanized mice with a recombinant wild-type strain MV expressing enhanced green fluorescent protein (EGFP), a strong EGFP signal was detected in the spleen, lymph nodes, and bone marrow. This fluorescence was confirmed to be associated with MV infection in human T and B cells. Furthermore, the mice exhibited leukopenia and rash-like green fluorescent foci reminiscent of a measles rash. These foci originated from the accumulation of human leukocytes adjacent to hair follicles, consistent with the pathology observed in non-human primate models. These results suggest that this small animal model could be a valuable tool for elucidating the mechanisms of MV infection and its pathogenicity.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Measles virus (MV) is a human pathogen with no naturally susceptible small animal model, limiting mechanistic studies of its pathogenicity. The study addressed the lack of suitable animal models by asking whether a humanized immune system mouse could recapitulate MV infection and disease features.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study established a small animal model using NOD/LtSz-scid/IL2Rγ null (NSG) immunodeficient mice implanted with human-cord-blood-derived CD34+ cells to evaluate MV infection. The aim was to assess the suitability of this model for studying MV pathogenicity.
analysis.methods: The authors infected humanized mice with a recombinant wild-type measles virus strain expressing enhanced green fluorescent protein (EGFP) and evaluated infection through fluorescence detection in tissues and assessment of clinical signs.
analysis.main_results: Upon infection, strong EGFP signals were detected in the spleen, lymph nodes, and bone marrow, confirmed to be associated with MV infection in human T and B cells. The mice exhibited leukopenia and rash-like green fluorescent foci consistent with measles pathology.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as evidence that the humanized mouse model recapitulates key features of MV infection and pathogenicity observed in non-human primates. They concluded that this model provides a valuable tool for elucidating MV mechanisms.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This model may enable mechanistic studies of MV pathogenesis, drug testing, and vaccine evaluation that were previously infeasible due to the lack of small animal models. It could also facilitate research into measles-associated complications.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to an abstract-only report, which restricts detailed methodological and result reporting. The strength of the evidence is low due to the absence of full methodological descriptions, sample sizes, statistical analyses, and comprehensive pathological assessments.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to address the lack of small animal models for measles virus (MV) by developing a humanized mouse model using NSG mice engrafted with human CD34+ cells. Upon infection with a recombinant MV expressing EGFP, the mice showed viral infection in human T and B cells in lymphoid tissues and developed leukopenia and rash-like lesions. The authors concluded that this model recapitulates key features of MV infection and pathogenicity seen in non-human primates, offering a potential tool for mechanistic studies. However, the evidence is limited to an abstract, providing no details on sample sizes, statistical methods, or comprehensive pathology, which constrains the strength of the findings.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 麻疹病毒 (MV) 是一种人类病原体,没有天然易感的小动物模型,限制了其致病性的机制研究。该研究通过询问人源化免疫系统小鼠是否可以重现 MV 感染和疾病特征,解决了缺乏合适动物模型的问题。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究使用植入人脐带血来源的 CD34+ 细胞的 NOD/LtSz-scid/IL2Rγ null (NSG) 免疫缺陷小鼠建立了小动物模型来评估 MV 感染。目的是评估该模型对于研究 MV 致病性的适用性。
elements_zh.methods: 作者用表达增强型绿色荧光蛋白 (EGFP) 的重组野生型 麻疹病毒 菌株感染人源化小鼠,并通过组织中的荧光检测和临床症状评估来评估感染情况。
elements_zh.main_results: 感染后,在脾脏、淋巴结和骨髓中检测到强 EGFP 信号,证实与人类 T 和 B 细胞中的 MV 感染有关。小鼠表现出白细胞减少症和皮疹样绿色荧光病灶,与 麻疹 病理学一致。

analysis_en.study_design_and_population: The study established a small animal model using NOD/LtSz-scid/IL2Rγ null (NSG) immunodeficient mice implanted with human-cord-blood-derived CD34+ cells to evaluate MV infection. title_zh: 麻疹病毒 感染会在人源化免疫系统小鼠模型中诱发白细胞减少症和皮疹
source_body_en: Abstract Humans are the natural hosts of the measles virus (MV). With the exception of non-human primates, no other animal species are naturally susceptible to MV infection. Thus, no small animal models exist to study the mechanisms of MV pathogenicity. The aim of the present study was to establish a small animal model of MV infection using NOD/LtSz-scid/IL2Rγ null (NSG) immunodeficient mice implanted with human-cord-blood-derived CD34 + cells and to evaluate its suitability as a measles model. Upon infecting the humanized mice with a recombinant wild-type strain MV expressing enhanced green fluorescent protein (EGFP), a strong EGFP signal was detected in the spleen, lymph nodes, and bone marrow. This fluorescence was confirmed to be associated with MV infection in human T and B cells. Furthermore, the mice exhibited leukopenia and rash-like green fluorescent foci reminiscent of a measles rash. These foci originated from the accumulation of human leukocytes adjacent to hair follicles, consistent with the pathology observed in non-human primate models. These results suggest that this small animal model could be a valuable tool for elucidating the mechanisms of MV infection and its pathogenicity.

title: The 2026 Measles Outbreak in Bangladesh: A Critique of Immunity Gaps and Care Deficiencies
abstract: Bangladesh entered 2026 amid a severe measles outbreak that peaked in mid-May. This article analyses the public health response to the outbreak and evaluates the government's management of the crisis. Health professionals and measles experts have attributed the outbreak to accumulated gaps in routine immunisation, weaknesses in public health infrastructure, poor nutritional status among children, widespread vitamin A deficiency, and maternal undernutrition during pregnancy and breastfeeding.

title: Barriers to disease notification among primary healthcare physicians in West Bank, Palestine: a cross-sectional survey
abstract: Abstract Introduction Underreporting remains a persistent challenge for infectious disease surveillance systems. Evidence on notification knowledge and practices among physicians in the West Bank remains limited, although they play a critical role in disease notification. We aimed to assess the knowledge, attitudes, and practices of primary healthcare physicians in disease notification, identify factors associated with appropriate notification of suspected mumps, measles, and chickenpox cases, and describe barriers to notification. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional survey on primary healthcare physicians in the Palestinian Ministry of Health primary healthcare centers between August 2024 and May 2025. The questionnaire assessed knowledge, attitudes, and self-reported notification practices. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify factors associated with recent notification practices. Results Among 223 respondents, 30.9% were categorized as having a good knowledge score of the disease notification process across multiple operational domains of disease notification, while 93.3% were categorized as having a good attitude score. Common misconceptions included laboratory confirmation being required for notification (61.0%) and that surveillance case definitions require laboratory criteria (65.5%). Over 80% of respondents notified their last-encountered measles, mumps, or chickenpox case. However, timely notification was lower; 52.4% of measles cases were reported immediately, compared with 19.3% of mumps and 14.0% of chickenpox cases reported within the recommended timeframes. Commonly reported barriers included lack of time (60.5%), and uncertainty about which diseases to notify (38.1%) and when (32.3%). Knowledge and attitude scores were not significantly associated with notification practices, although limited observations and composite scores may have obscured these associations. Physicians who received recent supervisory feedback on disease notification had higher odds of notifying chickenpox cases (OR: 4.01, 95%CI: 1.40-11.43). Compared to general practitioners, other medical specialties had lower odds of notifying mumps (OR: 0.21, 95%CI: 0.06–0.81) and chickenpox cases (OR: 0.23, 95%CI: 0.08–0.69). Conclusions Despite positive attitudes towards the notification system, knowledge gaps and misconceptions may contribute to underreporting of notifiable conditions. Strengthening training, clarifying guidance, improving feedback mechanisms, and addressing identified barriers and preferences may enhance disease notification performance by primary healthcare physicians in the West Bank.

title: ECHO: A lightweight tool for inferring missing case counts from pathogen phylogenies
abstract: AO_SCPLOWBSTRACTC_SCPLOWTimed phylogenetic trees express the evolutionary history of a pathogen outbreak in units of time, providing an estimate of the elapsed time across the shared ancestry of a set of taxa. By combining this elapsed time with known information about the epidemiology of a disease, we can relate the total branch length to the total number of cases related to the phylogeny. This gives information about the number of unsequenced cases that are related to the phylogeny. We call these "cryptic" cases. We present ECHO (Estimation of Cryptic Hosts from Outbreak trees), a collection of three lightweight estimators of the number of cryptic cases in a phylogeny. ECHO is agnostic to the form of the sampling process, making it robust to a variety of forms of sampling heterogeneity. We demonstrate ECHOs baseline accuracy and its robustness to heterogenous sampling frameworks through simulation. Additionally, we apply ECHO to measles virus sequences that were collected during an outbreak in the USA in 2021. ECHO is able to recover the number of cryptic cases with a reasonable degree of accuracy both in simulation and in practice. We discuss the contexts in which ECHO is most applicable, and the interpretation of its estimates.

analysis.research_question_and_background: Phylogenetic trees of pathogens provide evolutionary time scales but do not directly quantify unsequenced cases linked to an outbreak. The study addresses the knowledge gap in estimating the number of cryptic cases that are epidemiologically connected to sequenced samples but not represented in the phylogeny.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study introduces ECHO (Estimation of Cryptic Hosts from Outbreak trees), a tool comprising three lightweight estimators designed to infer missing case counts from timed phylogenetic trees. The authors demonstrate the tool’s performance through simulation and apply it to measles virus sequences collected during a 2021 outbreak in the USA.
analysis.methods: ECHO uses timed phylogenetic trees to relate total branch length to the total number of cases, thereby estimating cryptic cases. The tool is designed to be agnostic to sampling processes, ensuring robustness to heterogeneous sampling frameworks. Simulation studies and application to real-world measles virus data were used to evaluate accuracy.
analysis.main_results: ECHO recovered the number of cryptic cases with a reasonable degree of accuracy both in simulation and in practice when applied to measles virus sequences from the 2021 USA outbreak.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret ECHO’s estimates as providing actionable insights into the extent of cryptic transmission during outbreaks. The novelty lies in the development of a lightweight, sampling-agnostic tool specifically designed to infer missing case counts from phylogenetic data.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: ECHO can inform outbreak investigation and response by quantifying cryptic cases, thereby improving surveillance accuracy and guiding public health interventions for measles and potentially other pathogens with similar transmission dynamics.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The supplied evidence does not report the specific sample sizes, statistical confidence intervals, or detailed limitations beyond the tool’s agnosticism to sampling heterogeneity. The evidence strength is moderate, as the findings are supported by simulation and a single real-world application.

ECHO comprises three estimators and is robust to heterogeneous sampling frameworks. The tool was validated through simulation and applied to measles virus sequences from a 2021 USA outbreak, demonstrating reasonable accuracy in recovering cryptic case counts. The authors interpret the estimates as providing actionable insights into cryptic transmission. ECHO has potential public health significance by improving surveillance accuracy and guiding interventions for measles and similar pathogens.

title_zh: ECHO:一种轻量级工具,用于根据病原体系统发育推断缺失病例数
source_body_en: AO_SCPLOWBSTRACTC_SCPLOWTimed phylogenetic trees express the evolutionary history of a pathogen outbreak in units of time, providing an estimate of the elapsed time across the shared ancestry of a set of taxa. By combining this elapsed time with known information about the epidemiology of a disease, we can relate the total branch length to the total number of cases related to the phylogeny. This gives information about the number of unsequenced cases that are related to the phylogeny. We call these "cryptic" cases. We present ECHO (Estimation of Cryptic Hosts from Outbreak trees), a collection of three lightweight estimators of the number of cryptic cases in a phylogeny. ECHO is agnostic to the form of the sampling process, making it robust to a variety of forms of sampling heterogeneity. We demonstrate ECHOs baseline accuracy and its robustness to heterogenous sampling frameworks through simulation. Additionally, we apply ECHO to measles virus sequences that were collected during an outbreak in the USA in 2021. ECHO is able to recover the number of cryptic cases with a reasonable degree of accuracy both in simulation and in practice. We discuss the contexts in which ECHO is most applicable, and the interpretation of its estimates.

title: Strengthening Outbreak Response and Preparedness in US Health Departments Through a Community of Practice.
abstract: The reemergence of infectious diseases, such as measles, in the United States has placed significant strain on state, local, tribal, and territorial health departments to respond and contain the spread of disease. The actions by health departments have spanned a wide range of outbreak preparedness and response initiatives, with some health departments excelling in their approaches while others work to build capacity despite resource constraints. To strengthen outbreak preparedness and response, the Johns Hopkins Center for Outbreak Response Innovation convened a national Community of Practice series in 2025, bringing together 115 participants from 40 health departments. Presentations emphasized the importance of interdisciplinary collaboration, system adaptability, and continuous learning to enhance outbreak response capacity. This series underscored that sustainable improvements in public health practice rely on bridging academic research and operational realities through shared learning networks, ensuring that technical innovations translate into effective and scalable disease response strategies nationwide.
journal: Journal of public health management and practice : JPHMP

title: Routine early childhood vaccination uptake before and during the COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland: A population-based cohort study of administrative data.
abstract: OBJECTIVES: The COVID-19 pandemic changed the working patterns of many families and led to an increased focus on vaccines. This may have influenced early childhood vaccination uptake. We utilised linked administrative health data for Scotland to investigate whether the pandemic was associated with changes in uptake of early childhood vaccinations. STUDY DESIGN: Retrospective observational cohort design examining population-based individual-level linked administrative health data for Scotland. METHODS: We assessed timely uptake of six routine vaccinations - 6-in-1 vaccine, pneumococcal conjugate vaccine (PCV), rotavirus vaccine, Hib/MenC vaccine, measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) vaccine and PCV booster - among children reaching 12 months or 24 months of age in Scotland, January 2019-December 2021 (N = 199,574 children). Logistic regression modelling assessed uptake among a pandemic cohort compared to a pre-pandemic cohort, with and without adjustment for key sociodemographic variables. Interaction analysis assessed whether associations varied across area deprivation, parental socioeconomic class, urban-rural residence, and maternal ethnic group. RESULTS: Vaccination uptake either remained stable or increased for five of the six vaccines during the pandemic. Most interactions were not statistically significant, indicating broadly similar pandemic effects across sociodemographic groups. However, large pre-existing inequalities remained during the pandemic, with least-deprived areas and managerial/professional households having higher uptake, and several minority ethnic groups having lower uptake. CONCLUSIONS: Scotland's childhood immunisation programme showed resilience during the pandemic, but pre-existing inequalities persisted. Future planning should include safeguarding early-life vaccines and addressing structural barriers.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed whether the COVID-19 pandemic altered routine early childhood vaccination uptake in Scotland, motivated by observed changes in family working patterns and increased vaccine focus during the pandemic.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective observational cohort study used linked administrative health data for Scotland to examine population-based individual-level records of children reaching 12 or 24 months of age between January 2019 and December 2021 (N = 199,574 children).
analysis.methods: Timely uptake of six routine vaccinations was assessed using logistic regression to compare pandemic and pre-pandemic cohorts, with adjustment for sociodemographic variables and interaction analysis across area deprivation, parental socioeconomic class, urban-rural residence, and maternal ethnic group.
analysis.main_results: Vaccination uptake either remained stable or increased for five of the six vaccines during the pandemic, and most interaction terms were not statistically significant, indicating broadly similar effects across sociodemographic groups.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as evidence of resilience in Scotland’s childhood immunisation programme during the pandemic, while noting that large pre-existing inequalities persisted across socioeconomic and ethnic groups.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings suggest that routine early childhood vaccination programmes can maintain coverage during public health emergencies, but targeted strategies are needed to address structural barriers and reduce persistent inequalities.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study’s observational design and reliance on administrative data limit causal inference, and while the large sample size strengthens precision, unmeasured confounding and generalisability to other settings remain concerns.

analysis.summary_en: This population-based cohort study in Scotland evaluated whether the COVID-19 pandemic affected early childhood vaccination uptake by comparing pandemic and pre-pandemic cohorts using linked administrative health data for 199,574 children. Uptake remained stable or increased for five of six vaccines during the pandemic, with no significant sociodemographic interactions, indicating broadly uniform effects. However, large pre-existing inequalities persisted, particularly by area deprivation and maternal ethnic group. The authors conclude that Scotland’s immunisation programme showed resilience during the pandemic but highlight the need for safeguarding early-life vaccines and addressing structural barriers. The study’s observational design and administrative data limit causal inference, though the large sample size supports precision.

abstract_zh: 目标:COVID-19 大流行改变了许多家庭的工作模式,并导致人们更加关注 疫苗。这可能影响了儿童早期对 疫苗接种 的吸收。我们利用苏格兰的关联行政健康数据来调查该流行病是否与幼儿 疫苗接种 的吸收变化有关。研究设计:回顾性观察 队列研究 设计检查苏格兰基于人口的个人层面关联的行政健康数据。方法:我们评估了六种常规 疫苗接种 - 6 合 1 疫苗、肺炎球菌结合物 疫苗 (PCV)、轮状病毒 疫苗、Hib/MenC 疫苗、麻疹、腮腺炎和风疹 (MMR) 的及时摄取情况疫苗 和 PCV 加强剂 - 在苏格兰 12 个月或 24 个月大的儿童中,2019 年 1 月至 2021 年 12 月(N = 199,574 名儿童)。逻辑回归模型评估了大流行病 队列研究 与大流行前 队列研究 的吸收情况,并对关键社会人口统计学变量进行了调整和不调整。交互分析评估了关联是否因地区贫困、父母社会经济阶层、城乡居住地和母亲种族群体而异。结果:在大流行期间,六个 疫苗 中的五个的 疫苗接种 吸收率要么保持稳定,要么有所增加。大多数相互作用在统计上并不显着,这表明流行病对不同社会人口群体的影响大致相似。然而,在大流行期间,先前存在的巨大不平等现象仍然存在,最贫困地区和管理/专业家庭的接受程度较高,而一些少数民族群体的接受程度较低。结论:苏格兰的儿童免疫计划在大流行期间表现出弹性,但先前存在的不平等现象仍然存在。未来的规划应包括保护早期生命 疫苗 和解决结构性障碍。

title: Broad permissiveness of mammalian nectin-4 orthologs for morbilliviruses: a notable exception in dolphin nectin-4
abstract: Morbilliviruses utilize signalling lymphocytic activation molecule (SLAM) and nectin-4 as their major cellular receptors and exhibit distinct host specificities despite sharing common receptor usage. While species-specific differences in SLAM have been extensively investigated, the contribution of nectin-4 to morbillivirus host range remains poorly understood because nectin-4 is highly conserved among mammals. Here, we systematically compared the receptor activities of nectin-4 orthologs from human, dolphin, bat, dog and seal for representative morbilliviruses, including measles virus (MV), cetacean morbillivirus (CeMV), canine distemper virus (CDV), phocine distemper virus (PDV) and Myotis bat morbillivirus (MBaMV). Cell–cell fusion, virus infection and plaque assays demonstrated that most nectin-4 orthologs efficiently supported infection by all tested viruses. In contrast, dolphin nectin-4 exhibited markedly reduced receptor activity for MV, PDV and MBaMV, while remaining fully functional for CeMV and CDV. This phenotype was consistently observed with multiple clinical MV isolates. Mutational analyses identified amino acid residue 63 as a key determinant of this receptor specificity. Substitution of glutamic acid at position 63 in dolphin nectin-4 with glycine restored MV receptor activity to a level comparable to that of human nectin-4. These findings demonstrate that nectin-4 is generally a broadly permissive morbillivirus receptor but that specific amino acid differences can substantially influence receptor usage. Our results indicate that receptor compatibility contributes to morbillivirus host range and cross-species transmission while being insufficient on its own to fully explain viral host specificity.

title: Prevalence and factors associated with immunization non-completion among children aged 12–23 months at Kisoro General Hospital, Uganda: a cross-sectional study
abstract: Immunization non-completion, defined here as a child missing at least one age-appropriate vaccine dose under Uganda’s national immunization schedule (UNEPI), remains a critical public health problem in sub-Saharan Africa, exposing children to preventable diseases. In Uganda, coverage falls substantially below the WHO target of 90%, particularly in rural districts. This study determined the prevalence of immunization non-completion among children aged 12–23 months at Kisoro General Hospital and identified associated socio-economic and healthcare-related factors. A cross-sectional study was conducted from October to December 2024 at Kisoro General Hospital among 275 caregivers of children aged 12–23 months attending the immunization clinic, selected by systematic random sampling. Immunization non-completion was defined as failure to receive at least one age-appropriate dose per the UNEPI schedule (BCG, OPV, pentavalent, PCV, rotavirus, measles, and yellow fever vaccines) by 12–23 months of age. Data were collected via structured, pre-tested questionnaires and verified immunization card records. Descriptive statistics, bivariate chi-square tests, and multivariable logistic regression were performed using Stata version 15.1 (StataCorp, College Station, TX, USA). The participation rate was 90.5% (275/304). Caregivers who declined participation ( n = 10), were excluded after consent due to absent immunization records ( n = 12), or whose children fell outside the 12–23-month age range ( n = 7) are reported in full in the Results section. The prevalence of immunization non-completion was 34.2% (94/275; 95% CI: 28.5–39.8%). In multivariable analysis, significant predictors included lack of formal caregiver education (aOR = 3.3, 95% CI: 0.93–11.49; p = 0.044), delayed initiation of immunization beyond three weeks of birth (aOR = 7.3, 95% CI: 3.66–14.72; p < 0.001), unfriendly health worker attitude (aOR = 5.8, 95% CI: 1.29–11.46; p = 0.022), and vaccine stock-outs (aOR = 6.1, 95% CI: 1.71–14.67; p = 0.005). Children of caregivers aged 25–34 years were less likely to have incomplete immunization than those of caregivers aged over 34 years (aOR = 0.3, 95% CI: 0.16–0.76; p = 0.008). One in three children attending Kisoro General Hospital had incomplete immunization, far below national and global targets. Modifiable determinants at both caregiver and health system levels were identified. Targeted interventions including caregiver education, timely postnatal vaccination, health worker training, and vaccine supply strengthening are urgently needed.

abstract_original: Immunization non-completion, defined here as a child missing at least one age-appropriate vaccine dose under Uganda’s national immunization schedule (UNEPI), remains a critical public health problem in sub-Saharan Africa, exposing children to preventable diseases. In Uganda, coverage falls substantially below the WHO target of 90%, particularly in rural districts. This study determined the prevalence of immunization non-completion among children aged 12–23 months at Kisoro General Hospital and identified associated socio-economic and healthcare-related factors. A cross-sectional study was conducted from October to December 2024 at Kisoro General Hospital among 275 caregivers of children aged 12–23 months attending the immunization clinic, selected by systematic random sampling. Immunization non-completion was defined as failure to receive at least one age-appropriate dose per the UNEPI schedule (BCG, OPV, pentavalent, PCV, rotavirus, measles, and yellow fever vaccines) by 12–23 months of age. Data were collected via structured, pre-tested questionnaires and verified immunization card records. Descriptive statistics, bivariate chi-square tests, and multivariable logistic regression were performed using Stata version 15.1 (StataCorp, College Station, TX, USA). The participation rate was 90.5% (275/304). Caregivers who declined participation ( n = 10), were excluded after consent due to absent immunization records ( n = 12), or whose children fell outside the 12–23-month age range ( n = 7) are reported in full in the Results section. The prevalence of immunization non-completion was 34.2% (94/275; 95% CI: 28.5–39.8%). In multivariable analysis, significant predictors included lack of formal caregiver education (aOR = 3.3, 95% CI: 0.93–11.49; p = 0.044), delayed initiation of immunization beyond three weeks of birth (aOR = 7.3, 95% CI: 3.66–14.72; p < 0.001), unfriendly health worker attitude (aOR = 5.8, 95% CI: 1.29–11.46; p = 0.022), and vaccine stock-outs (aOR = 6.1, 95% CI: 1.71–14.67; p = 0.005). Children of caregivers aged 25–34 years were less likely to have incomplete immunization than those of caregivers aged over 34 years (aOR = 0.3, 95% CI: 0.16–0.76; p = 0.008). One in three children attending Kisoro General Hospital had incomplete immunization, far below national and global targets. Modifiable determinants at both caregiver and health system levels were identified. Targeted interventions including caregiver education, timely postnatal vaccination, health worker training, and vaccine supply strengthening are urgently needed.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted a cross-sectional analysis of immunization non-completion among children aged 12–23 months at Kisoro General Hospital in Uganda. It found that 34.2% of children had incomplete immunization, with significant predictors including lack of formal caregiver education, delayed initiation of immunization, unfriendly health worker attitudes, and vaccine stock-outs. The findings highlight the need for targeted interventions to improve immunization rates, such as caregiver education, timely postnatal vaccination, health worker training, and vaccine supply strengthening.
